title: Horse-drawn fire engines, Prohibition and the 1918 river flood
summary: Bailey recalls horse-drawn fire engines, the end of legal beer and speakeasies, and sandbagging a broken levee.

blocks.x: engine? Well that time they had the old horse and horse engine engine. They didn't have the automobile. Them did some of the old time of the engine horses. When they have a fire they had to have horses. The giant man be there at this station all night on their watch. When the fire come they have the harness all up in the adders and they just drop it on the horses and they go to the fire. Ain't no more to the stuff. The olden time. They have some of the beautiful horses you've ever seen in history. In giant horses. Did you ever hear any bands of any fire houses around you? Well no they had no bands no fire houses. And the men had to be on the leash for they work. Yeah well they have that today you know a couple of fire houses. Yeah they don't have that today. Today in giant has everything. Even today I see myself they even do their own cooking. But them days no cooking. Now you got the time of prohibition down here. When was that? Yeah it was in 1915 when the beer went out of existence. They had a local to call the Union Brewery in 161. That's everybody help them out to try to keep beer on. But it didn't exist. It went out of business. That's where the people went to work start to have them speakeasers. Making their own beer selling in hard spots. If you wouldn't know the spot to go in you couldn't get in. When you get in them speakeas you got to talk a lot. Because if you go to talking to the lodge, the lawyer you come in there and make a raise. That's town of prohibition. When that was this 1915. Now what about the river in 1918? You got something about the river? Well that was down in the country there. 1918 was a terrible time. The crow's vest broke. And he even had to get volunteer people to work. Trying to stop the water with sandbags. Keep them coming in the city.
